text:
The ultrasound findings of an enlarged, thin-walled gallbladder without stones, combined with significantly elevated alkaline phosphatase and jaundice, strongly suggest Courvoisier's sign, indicating a malignant obstruction of the common bile duct, likely pancreatic head cancer or cholangiocarcinoma. I will request further imaging to confirm the mass location and extent.

The normal hepatitis panel rules out viral hepatitis as the cause of your liver enzyme elevation. Given your significant alcohol use, elevated AST and ALT, and jaundice, I am concerned about alcoholic hepatitis or cirrhosis, despite the conflicting imaging.
